Metadata discovery: At session startup, agents scan configured scopes (such as project-level and user-level directories, e.g., `<project>/.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/`) for subdirectories containing a file named `SKILL.md`. Parsers extract YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`, and optional fields) and body content, storing records in an in-memory map keyed by `name`.

Progressive disclosure: Every skills-compatible agent follows a three-tier loading strategy:
- Tier 1 (Catalog): Name + description loaded at session start (~50-100 tokens per skill).
- Tier 2 (Instructions): Full `SKILL.md` body loaded when the skill is activated (<5000 tokens recommended).
- Tier 3 (Resources): Scripts, references, and assets loaded when instructions reference them.

Trust/permission boundaries: Project-level skills come from the repository being worked on, which may be untrusted. Consider gating project-level skill loading on a trust check (loading them only if the user marked the folder as trusted) to prevent untrusted repositories from silently injecting instructions. Additionally, if the agent uses a permission system for file access, allowlist skill directories so the model can read bundled resources without triggering user confirmation prompts.

Precedence advice: When two skills share the same `name`, apply the universal convention where project-level skills override user-level skills. Within the same scope, either first-found or last-found is acceptable (pick one and be consistent), and log a warning when a collision occurs so the user knows a skill was shadowed.

Skill loading/security related changes:
- **`/mnt/skills` is reserved** for managed enabled-only skill projections. `DEER_FLOW_HOST_SKILLS_PATH` / `SKILLS_HOST_PATH` are no longer used, and E2B operator mounts targeting that path are skipped with a warning. ([#4178](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4178))
- **A `SKILL.md` directory is a runtime package boundary** — nested `SKILL.md` files are supporting data, no longer registered as independent skills. ([#4098](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4098))
- **Skill review gate** — SkillScan now receives every file byte for byte (binaries, nested archives, and NUL bytes no longer escape scanning), archive extraction is capped by member count as well as size, and installer, export guard, and scanner share one code-file/executable-magic definition. ([#5431](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/5431), [ [#4241](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4241)])
- **Sandbox hardening** — local Docker sandboxes bind published ports to the Docker bridge gateway, run Docker's default seccomp profile, drop all capabilities, and get `no-new-privileges`; `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is scrubbed from the sandbox environment; and projected skill files are copies, not hardlinks, so a sandboxed write cannot mutate the canonical source. ([#4986](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4986), [ [#5145](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/5145)], [ [#4825](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4825)], [ [#4830](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4830)])
- **Secrets** — inherited secret environment variables are scrubbed from the skill environment; MCP stdio launcher arguments and env vars are constrained at the config API; credentials that cannot travel as HTTP header values are rejected at the config boundary; and skill toggles no longer persist resolved `$VAR` secrets into `extensions_config.json`. ([#4018](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4018), [ [#4617](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/4617)], [ [#5066](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/5066)], [ [#5357](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/5357)])
- **Authorization** — custom-Agent skill allowlists are enforced at the sandbox filesystem level. ([#5077](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/5077))
- **Skills & secrets** — toggling a skill no longer writes resolved secrets into `extensions_config.json`; restore `$VAR` references and rotate any credential exposed this way. ([#5357](https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/pull/5357))
